newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank sees room for further repo rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank sees room for further repo rate cuts.

text.p: Swedish Riksbank deputy governor Lars Heikensten said on Wednesday he believed there was still some room to reduce the central bank's key interest rate, the repo rate.

"The judgement we made in the middle of September that information available suggested that there was still some room to cut the repo rate remains unchanged," Heikensten said in an address to a financial seminar.
"On the other hand, you can't always assume that monetary policy will always follow a certain pattern in the future."
The repo rate currently stands at 4.95 percent but began the year at 8.91 percent. It has been lowered 21 times this year with the most recent move a cut of 10 basis points on Tuesday this week.

Heikensten said inflation in Sweden could develop more favourably than the central bank expected in its September inflation report and consumer price rises could stay within the Riksbank's one-three percent target range for the coming two years.
This, he said, was due to low inflation expectations and subdued inflationary pressure in the economy.
However, one thing that could complicate the situation was wage increases, the deputy governor said. The central bank said the rate of wage increases in the country as a whole exceeds five percent.
"This is not an acceptable rate in the long term," Heinkensten said.
He noted that the Swedish economy has been radically reevaluated over the past year and that international observers were now far more positive.

"You can call it a confidence shock if you like," he said. "Just as in earlier crises in the opposite direction this has had a dramatic effect on the conditions for monetary policy, primarily through the sharp appreciation of the crown it has caused."
